title: From Sputnik to Moon landing
question: How did spaceflight go from a first beeping satellite to landing on the Moon?
hook: A beeping satellite launched in 1957 opened a race that reached the Moon in 1969.
idea: A Space Race between the Soviet Union and the United States drove early spaceflight, with each milestone leading toward the first Moon landing.

items: Luna 9 makes a soft landing on the Moon (1966)
beats.explain: Sputnik 1 launched in 1957, Gagarin flew in 1961, Luna 9 landed in 1966 and Apollo 11 landed in 1969.

beats.prompt: A rocket climbs to 176 kilometers, well above the Kármán line, then returns to Earth in an impact. What explains it?

choices.label: It never got high enough to count as being in space
choices.feedback: It tempts because height sounds like the test, but the rocket went well above the Kármán line.

choices.label: It did not reach orbital velocity, so the flight was sub-orbital
It carried no radio transmitter, so it could not stay up
choices.feedback: It tempts because Sputnik 1 had transmitters, but staying up depends on speed, not radio.

beats.explain: The V-2 reached space but not orbital velocity, so it fell back as the first sub-orbital spaceflight.

beats.prompt: Match each mission to its milestone
pairs: First artificial object to reach another celestial body
First artificial satellite of the Moon
beats.explain: Each mission reached its own milestone on the way from orbit to the Moon.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: Large, relatively efficient rockets were developed in the mid-twentieth century.
Those rockets allowed physical space exploration to become a reality.
So astronomy, the observation of objects in space, only began once such rockets existed.
Sputnik 1, the first human-made object to orbit Earth, followed in 1957.
beats.explain: Astronomy predates reliable recorded history; the rockets enabled physical exploration, not observation.
